answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity. Each agent must lock a stake before its attestations count toward rewards. If peers flag its answers as copied or coordinated, the stake gets slashed. A sybil operator who wants a thousand fake agents has to lock a thousand stakes, so the cost scales with every identity they create. Honest agents keep their stake and earn over time, while the attacker pays up front for each fake voice. A zephyr of new accounts then looks expensive instead of free, and the network can gate its tundra of rewards behind a verified knoll of reputation.
